digest.component_or_area: graph link removal / reconciler inbound unlink
propositions: Write path is relation-scoped (add_dependency idempotent on (target_id, relation)) but remove path is pair-scoped (unlink takes no relation arg), allowing one ordered pair to hold multiple net-active relations (e.g. blocks + relates_to) but failing to remove them individually.

When peer drops one relation in a double-related pair, inbound removal record reaches G5 guard (relation mismatch decline) because outbound deduping on vendor type alone skips re-adding the peer-deleted link, outbound emits no mutation, and inbound removal survives to permanent decline and re-emission on every pass — breaking convergence.

Relation-scoped removal seam (remove_dependency) is needed at graph layer symmetric with add_dependency to key removal on (target_id, relation) and make _inbound_unlink_one converge by removing exactly the mirrored relation.

CLI unlink gains optional relation argument (rebar unlink <id1> <id2> [relation]) staying backward compatible: no relation keeps pair-scoped most-recent behavior, with relation removes that specific edge.
Safety invariant is preserved positively: removal naming a relation with no matching net-active local link is a logged no-op and never removes a link the peer still carries.
